rationale: The successor fixed experiment executed (CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568, completed/tests_passed) and its parsed events match the raw stdout line for line, so the gap and the mis-specified control from the parent receipt can now be settled with evidence instead of argument. I record the measured window bound (the leader's next real heartbeat restores the context and the identical pre-vote is ignored again), the quorum-scale consequence (a single forged delivery to the other voter let an up-to-date candidate win the pre-vote, the vote and the leadership at term 3 while the incumbent still reported leadership at term 2), the re-specified local-API control, and a Fact carrying the observation. The parent question's current account is updated to fold both receipts in, the gap is answered with resolved=true, and the still-unexecuted aftermath (the incumbent's demotion and log continuity once the new leader's messages arrive) is registered as a new child question so the bounded prefix is not mistaken for the whole picture.

investigations.question: After the forged path has produced a second leader at a higher term, does the incumbent step down correctly when the new leader's MsgApp/MsgHeartbeat arrive, and does the new leader's log contain every entry committed under the incumbent (no divergence or lost commitment), so the harm is bounded to the unnecessary leadership change rather than log-integrity loss?
investigations.hypothesis: Delivering the new leader's term-3 MsgApp to node 1 makes it become a follower at term 3 (stepFollower sets lead=1 and handleAppendEntries matches at (index=11, term=2)), so the incumbent's authority is shed by the ordinary higher-term rule, while the new leader's log already contains the entries committed under the incumbent.
investigations.discriminator: Extend group B by feeding node 3's post-election MsgApp and heartbeats to node 1 and observing node 1's soft state and the new leader's log prefix; a clean transfer with the committed prefix intact bounds the defect to disruption, whereas any index/term mismatch or entry loss would widen it to a safety defect.

knowledge.statement: In a three-voter group, one peer-form MsgForgetLeader delivered to the single other voter (node 2) is enough for an up-to-date candidate (node 3) to win the pre-vote, win the real vote and become StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent node 1 still reports StateLeader at term 2 with its term-2 entry committed; the incumbent answered neither the pre-vote nor the vote request (its own lease suppressed both), and once the leader's next real heartbeat was processed the follower's context was restored and the identical pre-vote was ignored again.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 5-8 and 13-18 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, voters {1,2,3} with a shared log at index=10/term=1 and entry 11 replicated from leader 1; the incumbent was not fed the new leader's messages, so its demotion path is outside this observation; no follower was ticked except the leader, so follower election timeouts did not fire.

interpretations.rationale: Current account with both receipts folded in. A MsgForgetLeader sent by a peer in wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) reaches the follower state machine through RawNode.Step, is accepted with no error, and clears the live leader context (Lead 1 -> 0) - witnessed first at index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 and reproduced at index 5 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568. It changes the support the follower gives an up-to-date candidate's pre-vote: the identical request that produced no response while the lease held (under-lease controls at indices 3/4 of the first receipt and 4/10 of the second) is granted afterwards (indices 5 of the first, 6/14 of the second). The second receipt extends that to the cluster level: one such message to the other voter was enough for the follower to grant the real vote (index 15) and for the candidate to become StateLeader at term 3 (index 17) while the incumbent still reported StateLeader at term 2 (index 18), i.e. a healthy leader is replaced without the quorum-wide external evidence the ForgetLeader contract requires; the window opened per follower is closed by the next genuine leader message (indices 7/8), and the local API still produces the same state change legitimately (index 2), which is exactly why the inbound path must not. Cause and controls are unchanged from the first account: the type is absent from isLocalMsg even though its only producers are the local ForgetLeader APIs and, with no term field, Step treats it as a local message and performs no term check; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected (indices 2 first / 3 second). Scope limits stand: one delivered message clears one follower's context, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refuses the change, the deposit of the incumbent depends on the new leader's messages reaching it (child question @forged_forget_aftermath), and no entry loss or log divergence was observed, so this is a disruption/authority-transition defect rather than an integrity defect.

ce33f7b508af4244883ac9c81a2a4696-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568: the window lasts until the next genuine leader message (restoring heartbeat at index 7, identical pre-vote ignored again at index 8, one leader tick with HeartbeatTick=1), and a quorum-scale election did follow the forged delivery (granted pre-vote index 14, granted vote index 15, candidate StateLeader at term 3 index 17 while the incumbent still reported leadership at term 2 at index 18).

counterevidence: The strongest competing explanation for the grants - that this follower grants pre-votes and votes to any up-to-date candidate regardless of the leader - is excluded by the under-lease controls in both receipts (no response at all while the context was intact).

The change is reversible and per-message: the next genuine leader heartbeat restored the context and the same pre-vote was ignored again (indices 7, 8), so the defect does not survive a communicating leader.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the documented inbound path; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test.
Observation is single-process with hand-delivered messages; no wall-clock duration or multi-host transport behaviour is measured.
The incumbent's demotion after the forged election is not observed (registered as @forged_forget_aftermath), and no other voter was fooled in the quorum scenario.
interpretations.joint_history: The two receipts are separate executions of the same fixed-experiment lineage, not fragments of one run: CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 (experiment ce33f7b508af4244883ac9c81a2a4696-experiment) is the parent harness, and CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568 (experiment acc6241dce584bc0a6817149dbe19f98-experiment, previous_id = the parent) is a revised basis that kept the parent scenario byte-for-byte in behaviour and added events. Both run in the same package with the same construction prefix (three real RawNode instances built from MemoryStorage snapshots at index=10/term=1 with voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, a real election for node 1 and a real replicated term-2 entry) and print into their own runner streams, so neither depends on the other's observations. Their cited indices are compatible but not interchangeable: the parent stream's events 2-5 are the same observations as the successor's events 3-6 (inbound_local_msg, prevote_outcome under_lease, inbound_forget_leader, prevote_outcome after_forget) with identical field values, the successor merely adds heartbeat_delivered_node3 and local_forget_leader_api ahead of them; the successor additionally supplies the new repair-path and quorum-group observations that the parent stream never contained. Nothing in the combined account is derived by joining bytes across the two runs; each cited index is read from its own receipt.
